ticket: CH-01 — Ephemeral scoped MCP credentials for first-party chat
goal: Give the first-party "Ask Sayre" agent loop a short-lived, conversation-bound, digest-only MCP bearer credential whose effective RBAC scope is exactly the asking user's own effective scope, so the existing MCP gateway and every existing tool handler enforce that user's access with zero handler changes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: mintEphemeralMcpCredential returns a one-time bearer token matching /^mcp_chat_[a-f0-9]{16}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/, and presenting that token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the real gateway (POST /mcp through createMcpGatewayRouter with the real resolveMcpCredential) inside its TTL authenticates successfully and serves a tool call.

The resolved credential's effective read scope has identical resource coverage to the issuing user's current effective scope from PostgresPermissionStore.getReadScope — proven by canReadResource agreeing on every probe resource for the mint-time ceiling intersected with the issuer's live scope.

A token presented after expiresAt is rejected with McpKeyAuthenticationError, and the gateway response for it is byte-identical to the response for a syntactically valid but entirely unknown token (HTTP 401, {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Unauthorized."},"id":null}) — no expired-vs-unknown oracle.

Storage is digest-only: the payload handed to the store contains no substring of the returned token's secret, keyHmac matches /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/ and equals mcpSecretHmac(secret, pepper), and pepperVersion is the configured version. No persisted column and no returned audit field carries the raw token.

The persisted ceiling is exactly the issuing user's mint-time effective scope (allows as effect:'allow' rows, denies as effect:'deny' rows, subject_type='agent_key', subject_id=<key prefix>), and a ceiling artificially widened after mint still cannot produce coverage beyond the issuer's live scope, because resolution intersects the two.

Audit fields are persisted and queryable: listEphemeralMcpCredentialAudit returns kind, conversationId, issuedByUserId, issuedByLabel, issuedAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt for a conversation, org-scoped, with no digest or key material in the result.

TTL defaults to 300 seconds when ttlSeconds is omitted, is accepted up to 600 seconds, and is rejected above 600 or when non-integer/non-positive — rejected before any key material is generated or any row is written. The 600-second ceiling is additionally enforced in the database by mcp_client_keys_ephemeral_ttl_check.

org_id is never accepted from caller input: mintEphemeralMcpCredential's signature has no org parameter, the input object's accepted key set is exactly conversationId/ttlSeconds, and every write runs inside withOrgContext(db, ctx.orgId, ...).

For an ephemeral credential the rate-limit and metric bucket key is chat:<issuing user id>, so a second credential minted for the same user continues consuming the same per-minute window rather than a fresh one; for an agent key the bucket key is still the key prefix and behavior is unchanged.

Existing agent-key behavior is unchanged end to end (issue, resolve, revoke, rate-limit settings), and the admin surfaces exclude the new family: getMcpKeySettings never returns a chat_ephemeral row, and revokeMcpKey given a chat_ephemeral credential's id throws McpKeyNotFoundError.
No file under services/core/src/mcp/handlers/, nor services/core/src/graph-query/permissions.ts, nor services/core/src/mcp/gateway.ts, nor services/core/src/auth/context.ts appears in the diff.

sweepExpiredEphemeralMcpCredentials deletes expired chat_ephemeral rows together with their permissions rows, within one org and one transaction, leaving live ephemeral rows, every agent row (expired or not), and every other org untouched; it is rejected for a non-user or non-admin context; and it is not wired to any scheduler in this ticket.

Migration 0019 follows repo convention: hand-authored SQL with --> statement-breakpoint separators, a matching meta/_journal.json entry, the three CHECK constraints, both partial indexes, and a DROP-then-CREATE of resolve_mcp_client_key that remains SECURITY DEFINER with SET search_path = public, pg_temp and re-applies REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC / GRANT EXECUTE ... TO sayre_app.

edgeCases.text: A syntactically valid token with an unknown prefix is rejected identically to an expired one — same error type, same gateway status and body.
Expiry boundary: a token used when now === expiresAt is rejected (<=); one used 1 ms earlier is accepted.

Token-family / stored-kind mismatch in both directions — an mcp_chat_ token whose row is kind='agent', and an mcp_live_ token whose row is kind='chat_ephemeral' — is rejected before the HMAC comparison.
An unrecognized kind value in the database maps to null and is rejected; it never degrades to 'agent'.

Malformed tokens (no '.' separator, wrong prefix literal, non-hex prefix body, prefix body of wrong length, secret of wrong length or with disallowed characters, empty string, whitespace-only, missing Bearer scheme) are rejected by parseToken with no store lookup at all.
An ephemeral row whose pepper_version differs from the configured version is rejected (rotation invalidates in-flight ephemeral credentials — acceptable at a 300s TTL).
An ephemeral row with revoked_at set is rejected, even though this ticket ships no revocation surface.

The issuing user is deleted after mint: the ON DELETE SET NULL cascade succeeds (the DB CHECK deliberately does not require created_by), the credential then fails authentication on createdBy === null, and getReadScope returns the empty scope.
ttlSeconds of 0, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, 601, '300', null, or true is rejected; omitting the key yields 300.
conversationId that is missing, empty, a non-UUID string, a non-string, or accompanied by any extra/unknown key on the input object is rejected.

A non-user caller — including a resolved ephemeral credential's own subjectType:'agent_key' context — cannot mint another credential (no self-issuance chain), and cannot read audit rows or run the sweep.

An issuing user with an empty effective scope mints successfully: zero permissions rows are written, the credential resolves, and every tool returns empty/null rather than an error that would leak the caller's scope emptiness.
An owner issuer's ceiling is the single wildcard rule {repoId: null, branch: null, pathPrefix: null}; the resolved coverage equals the owner scope and is not broadened.
The issuer's permissions are narrowed, or a deny is added, after mint but before use: the very next resolve narrows accordingly (live intersection), with no new mint required.
A ceiling permissions row edited directly in the database to something broader than the issuer's live scope still yields no additional authorized resource.
An issuer whose effective scope exceeds MAX_EPHEMERAL_CEILING_ROWS rules causes mint to fail loudly rather than silently persisting a truncated (narrower) ceiling.
Two concurrent mints for the same conversationId both succeed with distinct prefixes and independent expiries — there is no unique constraint on conversation_id.
Minting a second credential for the same user does not reset the per-minute rate-limit window; two different users each get their own window; agent keys keep per-prefix windows.
getMcpKeySettings omits chat_ephemeral rows entirely, and revokeMcpKey given such a row's id throws McpKeyNotFoundError rather than revoking it.

Database CHECK constraints reject: a chat_ephemeral row with NULL conversation_id; a chat_ephemeral row with NULL expires_at; a chat_ephemeral row with expires_at > created_at + 600s or expires_at <= created_at; an agent row with a non-null conversation_id; and any row with a kind outside the two allowed values.

deleteExpired is org-scoped and kind-scoped: it removes only expired chat_ephemeral rows plus their permissions rows, and leaves live ephemeral rows, expired agent keys, and other orgs' rows in place.

No raw token reaches any persisted column, metric attribute, error message, thrown stack, or log line; error messages for every rejection path are the fixed constant strings defined on the error classes.
After 0019, resolve_mcp_client_key(text) is not executable by PUBLIC, is executable by sayre_app, and retains SECURITY DEFINER plus SET search_path = public, pg_temp.

Audit read scoping: a member sees only credentials they themselves issued for that conversation; an owner/admin sees all of that conversation's credentials within their org; a conversation id belonging to another org returns an empty array (RLS + explicit org_id predicate), never another tenant's rows.
